findings.title: PRD §4 Storage still specifies the per-session-DB architecture that DECISIONS-r3 Q6/Q7 replaced
findings.number: 17 lines (PRD-v2.md:68-84) describe per-session files (sessions/<server-id>.db, 'single writer', 'No shared writable DB', 'doctor --fix deletes only that session DB'). This is not the 2 lines BOTTLENECKS-r4 item 3 flagged (PRD-v2.md:84,173); it is the whole storage section those 2 lines sit inside.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:68-84 (tree shows `sessions/<server-id>.db content index of ONE MCP connection — single writer`, then '**Write:** only the owner writes its file. No shared writable DB'). Contrast docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md (accepted, Q6/Q7 in DECISIONS-r3.md): one shared `context.db` per project, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, multi-writer tested in tickets/verify-single-db.md (8 writers, 0 busy errors). git archaeology: v1 never had a shared DB — `git log --oneline -S withRetry -- src/db-base.ts` in cm-main shows the per-DB SQLITE_BUSY retry path added at 13dcec21 ('fix: handle SQLITE_BUSY with retry logic and graceful errors (closes #218)') and reworked through f6c61535/065799f8 for the single-writer-per-file model; the shared-file model is new in v2 and only ADR-0002 states it.
findings.why_it_blocks: M1 Core (store, sandbox, lifecycle, tools + contract tests) is the first milestone and every later milestone (M2 reference adapters, M3 nine more hook/MCP adapters, M4 plugin adapters, M5 CLI+stats) is built against the storage contract M1 produces. If an engineer or agent implements M1 from PRD §4 as written, they build per-session files, migrate ADR-0002's corruption/retention rules onto a layout that no longer exists, and every downstream milestone inherits the wrong contract. This is the single highest-leverage doc bug in the set: fixing only PRD-v2.md:84/173 (as r4 item 3 does) leaves the surrounding architecture description wrong.
findings.fix: Rewrite PRD-v2.md §4 end to end to match ADR-0002: one `context.db` per project (sha256(git-common-dir)), multi-writer via BEGIN IMMEDIATE, rename-aside corruption recovery (not delete), `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` MCP tools (not a CLI command). Keep `owners/<server-id>.pid` only if ADR-0002 still names per-server liveness tracking separately from the data file; state that explicitly so the two don't look like two live architectures.

findings.title: ADR-0016 case B/C indexes full large output on the server synchronously, with no worker-thread or chunking step — contradicts the harness's own measured advice
findings.number: tickets/verify-single-db.md point 6: '1 MB index tx p50 24 ms, p99 108 ms' and the explicit warning 'big indexing writes on the server still block JS while they wait. Run them in a worker thread or in small chunks.' ADR-0016 names 0 worker-thread or chunking mechanism for the case B/C index step.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0016-subagent-context-protection.md case B: 'indexes the full output in context.db ... then prints the chunks that best match the intent' — this indexing runs inline in the deny-rewrite / PostToolUse-replace path, i.e. on the MCP server's main thread, for every subagent call whose output would otherwise flood context (the ADR's own example is a 5 MB curl response, GP3 golden case). tickets/verify-single-db.md:48 names the fix ('worker thread or small chunks') for exactly this shape of write but ADR-0016 does not cite or apply it. grep -rn 'worker' docs/v2/adr/*.md returns nothing.
findings.why_it_blocks: The MCP server is one process serving every agent's hook calls (10 agents per PRD-v2 M3/M4 scope). A single subagent that triggers case B/C on a multi-MB output blocks the event loop for up to the ~108 ms p99 per MB measured, multiplied by output size (a 5 MB curl body is 5x the measured 1 MB unit) — during that window every other agent's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook on the same server stalls, not just the one that produced the large output. This is a cross-agent bottleneck the hook-latency budgets (GS6/GP3) do not account for because they measure single-call latency, not what one agent's large-output call does to the others.
findings.fix: Name a worker-thread (or child-process) indexing path for the case B/C write in ADR-0016, matching verify-single-db.md's own recommendation, and add a GP3 case that runs case B on a 5 MB output while a second simulated agent's hook call is in flight, asserting the second call's wall time is not inflated by the first's indexing.

findings.title: M2 is a single point of failure for the whole milestone plan and has no owner-approval gate named, unlike M7
findings.number: M2 ('hook runtime, journal, policy, CC + Codex') sits between M1 and 8 of the milestone's remaining items (M3's 10 adapters + M4's 4 plugin adapters depend on the hook runtime and journal format M2 fixes). PRD-v2.md names an explicit owner-approval gate for M7 ('needs your approval') and S0/S1 spikes for M0, but 0 gate or review checkpoint for M2 even though it is the widest fan-out point in the plan.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:213-220 (M0-M7 list). M3 lists 10 named agents, M4 lists 4; all of them build on 'hook runtime, journal, policy' from M2 per the dependency order stated in the same list. No review/approval step is named between M2 and M3's start, unlike M7's explicit 'needs your approval'.
findings.why_it_blocks: Per the owner's rule to run git-archaeology-informed decisions through /context-mode-ops before committing to a design, a hook-runtime or journal format choice made at M2 that turns out wrong is discovered only after M3+M4's 14 adapters are already built against it, because nothing forces a checkpoint. This is the most expensive place in the plan for a late-discovered defect.
findings.fix: Add an explicit owner review checkpoint at the end of M2, before M3 starts, naming what must be confirmed (hook runtime contract, journal schema, policy decision shape) — the same kind of gate already named for M7.
